Abstract:

In recent years, the proliferation of traffic surveillance infrastructure and the enormous
volume of video data generated by such systems have opened up new opportunities for
intelligent and automated traffic monitoring solutions. In this context, there is an increasing
interest in computer vision-based methods that can transform conventional surveillance
systems into intelligent platforms for real-time traffic law enforcement and road safety
monitoring. Among the various traffic violations that warrant automated monitoring, failure
to wear a seat belt is a significant concern, considering its direct correlation with the
severity of injuries sustained during vehicular accidents. Consequently, research efforts are
increasingly directed towards developing robust automated systems for seat belt detection.
However, several visual challenges, including non-uniform illumination, windshield glare,
motion-induced occlusions, and low visual contrast between seat belts and vehicle interiors,
complicate reliable detection in real-world traffic surveillance environments.
This dissertation aims to develop an intelligent traffic surveillance framework for
automated seat belt compliance detection in video data. The research employs deep
learning methodologies to extract and classify seat belt features, progressively advancing
from lightweight convolutional architectures to advanced feature fusion and attention-based
detection frameworks specifically tailored for detecting thin objects under challenging visual
conditions.
